beats.care: Four of five cases involved people aged 65–80. Tell parents and grandparents: hang up and call 1930.
beats.what: Callers posed as TRAI staff and a fake IPS officer. They threatened a money-laundering 'arrest' on video calls.
beats.why: Police traced money to a suspected mule account in Hyderabad and found five more people paying into it.

cards.body: A caller says your Aadhaar-linked SIM was misused abroad. A 'police officer' joins on video, threatens arrest, and pushes you to pay, pledge gold or break FDs.

cards.q: Someone on a video call says you're under 'digital arrest'. What's true?
cards.why: Delhi Police say digital arrest doesn't exist; real officials never ask for money on video calls.

hook: Would your parents *spot a fake police video call*?

learn.t: There is no such thing as a 'digital arrest'. Real officers never demand money on video calls.
